courses.title: Environmental Science Laboratory
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to environmental science as a branch of the sciences, encompassing the scientific method and its application within both laboratory and field settings. It examines the application of scientific, environmental, ecological, and sustainability principles in relation to human societies.
courses.advisories: ENGL C1000 or ENGL C1000H or ESL D005.

courses.title: Environmental Science
courses.description: This introductory course explores the relationships between human activities and the environment, examining their impacts on living and nonliving systems. Course topics include evolution, ecology, biodiversity, human population dynamics, resource use, pollution, environmental degradation, climate change, management of marine and freshwater resources, and environmental policy.

courses.title: Environmental Biology
courses.description: This course serves as an introduction to environmental biology as a branch of the environmental sciences and its relation to the scientific field. It will review the principles of environmental biology, ecology, and conservation as they relate to natural resource use, the biodiversity crisis, pollution, human population, climate change, and the impacts on all cultural, ethnic, and gender groups. Field trips outside scheduled class time may be required for this course.
